summary: Describes how to configure and execute bulk promotion of all eligible students from one academic session to the next, providing a report on the promotion outcome.

Configuration: Navigate to "Student" -> "Student Session Management" -> "Student Session Management Config".
Click to create a new configuration for student session management.

Define the promotion rule for each class by selecting 'From Class', 'From Batch' (if applicable), 'From Category', 'To Class', 'To Section', 'To Category' (always "Old" for promoted students), and 'Promoted Status' ("Simple Promote" or "Promoted with Dues").
Repeat this process for all classes that need to be promoted (e.g., LKG to UKG, Class 1 to Class 2, etc.).
Execution: Select the 'To Session' (e.g., 25-26) in the pop-up window.
Wait for the process to complete; a success message will indicate when the report file will be ready.
Reporting: Download the generated Excel report file.
Review the report for 'Total Count', 'Added Count', 'Updated Count', and 'Skipped Count' with reasons.

business_rules: Bulk promotion operates based on the configurations defined in "Student Session Management Config".
The 'To Category' for all promoted students is always "Old".
For schools, "Promoted with Dues" is typically preferred; for colleges, "Simple Promote" is common. This choice must be confirmed with the client.
If sections are to be combined during promotion (e.g., Class 1A and 1B to Class 2A), this must be confirmed by the institute.
Inactive students are automatically excluded from bulk promotion.
Promotion will be skipped for students if the fee structure for their target class/session is not set up.
important_notes: Bulk promotion is the most efficient method for promoting a large student body.
The report file provides an overview of the promotion results; for detailed verification, export student data and use tools like VLOOKUP.
If a single class requires different 'Promoted Status' (with/without dues) for different students, bulk promotion cannot handle this; manual promotion must be used for those specific students.
